title: Example 19-4: Embedded Transcriber’s Note

illustrates.quote: g. Enclose the transcriber-assigned column letters/row numbers, and the number of letters in the word, in an embedded transcriber’s note.

blocks.features: Verified against the PDF page image (p.521): print shows only "1. Parent’s female child"; the "(a1) (8)" (transcriber-assigned column/row + letter count) exists only in the braille, per 19.5.2e/f/g. Decoded from the given braille: the column/row designator "a1" is plain text inside the embedded note, while the letter-count "(8)" is separately parenthesized inside that SAME note (BRF opening/closing parenthesis "<"/">", confirmed against the symbols appendix, source line 18498) — both enclosed in ONE embedded transcriber's note (@.<...@.>) immediately after the clue, on the same line. Emboss has no inline/embedded-note mechanism (F-221), so this is built as plain appended text; expect the model's own output to be missing the TN enclosure marks around "a1 (8)".

print.notes: A single numbered crossword clue, illustrating the embedded-transcriber's-note construct of 19.5.2e-g.
print.printFeatures: Plain numbered list item; print itself carries none of the column/row/count annotation.

braille.notes: Byte-identical between run A and run B, and independently re-derived from source-line 15131. Decoded: '#a4' = '1.'; ',p>5t's female *' = "Parent's female child" ('*' = the one-cell 'ch' whole-word sign, i.e. 'child'); '@.<a#a "<#h">@.>' = an embedded transcriber's note reading 'a1 (8)'.

resolution: Braille unchanged (A and B agree; independently re-derived and decoded). Print side: reconciled to what the PDF page image actually shows (just the clue, no column/row/count annotation) plus a documented decode of the embedded note's own content, appended to the clue text since Emboss has no embedded-note mechanism to build it properly (F-221).
